s: The abstract concerns Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and its use with Large Language Models (LLMs). It identifies query-unsuitability as a cause of erroneous retrieved context and knowledge-boundary limitations as a cause of answers inconsistent with external references. s: The unit explains how Large Language Models support question answering but can produce hallucinations caused by factual errors and knowledge limitations. The authors introduce CoV-RAG, which uses a Chain-of-Verification to assess references and answers, revise queries, re-retrieve information, and improve generation during training and inference. Experiments on four public datasets report improved factuality across multiple models and retrieval tools.
